account.notes: Proposed in the FY2026 and FY2027 budget requests only; never reported by a committee or enacted (P.L. 119-75 has no such heading). The committee tables print it only in the request column, as the request's funding 'not displayed under other HHS accounts below' (H.Rept. 119-271 p.334 footnote 1/): the tables show most of the proposed AHA under HRSA, SAMHSA and the other legacy lines. observations.source_table_or_section: Title II, ACC-HHS-HRSA-TOTAL -- printed as 'Total, Health Resources and Services Administration' 8,286,229 [FY 2025 Estimate], PDF p.340 (printed p.336). Source: H.Rept. 119-271's 'FY 2025 Estimate' column, which the report defines (pp.319-320) as 'FY 2025 Operating Plans and other available information'; FY2025 was a full-year continuing resolution (P.L. 119-4, Full-Year Continuing Appropriations Act, 2025, division A). P.L. 119-4 sec. 1109(a): amounts necessary to maintain program levels -- no dollar level in law; this is the report's estimate. Parts the law does set: P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(2), 139 Stat. 33: HRSA-Wide Activities and Program Support, '"$0" for "$890,788,000"' (with $219,588,000 for $1,110,376,000).

validation.resolution: Owner decision: FY2025 was funded by a full-year CR (P.L. 119-4) with no dollar level; the enacted figure is the FY2026 House report's FY2025 estimate, as decided earlier. The FY2025 (CR) column label discloses this.

absence.evidence: P.L. 119-4 (Full-Year Continuing Appropriations Act, 2025, division A) provides no Adoption Incentives rescission for FY2025. Deciding text, sec. 1101(a)(8) (139 Stat. 11; PDF p. 3; text layer): it continues 'The Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2024 (division D of Public Law 118-47), except section 240 shall be applied by substituting "$1,471,000,000" for "$1,250,000,000" ..., except sections 241 and 310, ...'. Section 241 of that division (P.L. 118-47, 138 Stat. 681) is the FY2024 rescission of $70,000,000 of P.L. 117-328 Children and Families Services Programs funds 'for grants to States for incentive payments, as defined by section 473A of the Social Security Act' -- the line the FY2024 tables print as 'Adoption Incentives (rescission)' -70,000. Sec. 1105 continues the referenced Acts' provisions only 'Except as otherwise expressly provided in this division'. The Labor-HHS title of the CR (title IX, secs. 1901-1912, 139 Stat. 31-33) adds no such rescission, and the whole law's text layer has no 'adoption', '473A' or 'incentive payments'. No committee table covers FY2025 Enacted (H.Rept. 119-271's 'FY 2025 Estimate' column is operating plans, held back).

Not in the FY2021 or FY2022 bills, Budget Appendix language or laws (searched for '1820(c)(2)(B)' and 'distance requirement'). Its confirmed absences, which rested on tables' silence, were retired 2026-10-08 (owner).

The House counts the HHS rescissions (NEF, Adoption Incentives) in Title II's general provisions; the Senate prints them after the grand total, outside Title II -- so the two FY2024 figures differ by 1,320,000 as printed.

observations.source_table_or_section: Title II, ACC-HHS-TITLE-II-TOTAL -- printed as 'Total, Title II, Department of Health and Human Services' 1,300,549,900 [FY 2025 Estimate], PDF p.365 (printed p.361). Source: H.Rept. 119-271's 'FY 2025 Estimate' column, which the report defines (pp.319-320) as 'FY 2025 Operating Plans and other available information'; FY2025 was a full-year continuing resolution (P.L. 119-4, Full-Year Continuing Appropriations Act, 2025, division A). P.L. 119-4 sec. 1109(a): amounts necessary to maintain program levels -- no dollar level in law; this is the report's estimate. Parts the law does set: P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(2), 139 Stat. 33: HRSA-Wide Activities and Program Support, '"$0" for "$890,788,000"' (with $219,588,000 for $1,110,376,000); P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(3), 139 Stat. 33: SAMHSA Health Surveillance and Program Support, '"$0" for "$72,090,000"'; P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(4), 139 Stat. 33: ACF Children and Families Services Programs, '"$0" for "$40,011,000"'; P.L. 119-4 sec. 1908(5), 139 Stat. 33: ACL Aging and Disability Services Programs, '"$0" for "$29,268,000"'; P.L. 119-4 sec. 1902(b), 139 Stat. 31: HCFAC level '$941,000,000' (+24,000 +1,000 +1,000 over Div. D); P.L. 119-4 sec. 1101(a)(8), 139 Stat. 11: Div. D sec. 240 continued 'by substituting "$1,471,000,000" for "$1,250,000,000"'; P.L. 119-4 sec. 1109(b)(2), 139 Stat. 13: Medicaid advance for 1st quarter FY2026 '$261,063,820,000'. H.Rept. 119-271 counts the HHS rescissions (Nonrecurring Expenses Fund) inside Title II (House scope), unlike the FY2024 figures recorded from S.Rept. 118-207.

validation.resolution: Owner decision: FY2025 was funded by a full-year CR (P.L. 119-4) with no dollar level; the enacted figure is the FY2026 House report's FY2025 estimate, as decided earlier. The FY2025 (CR) column label discloses this.

Equals the P.L. 119-4 level in the House scope: Scope only: B - A = -1,471,000 is exactly the FY2025 NEF rescission, which H.Rept. 119-271 counts inside Title II (House scope) and the S.Rept. 118-207 FY2024 baseline leaves out (Senate scope).
